title: Adaptive failover delay and sticky-tenant probing hotfix
author: Rohit Gupta
description:
Context: During a regional failover incident we observed rapid reopen / rejoin attempts from the controller side that caused KV pressure spikes and circuit flapping for tenants that had recently been evicted. This PR introduces two coordinated mitigations: 1) an adaptive failover delay that increases the regional rejoin backoff dynamically based on KV pressure and recent reopen history, and 2) a sticky-tenant probing policy that ensures evicted tenants are probed on a low-frequency, exponential backoff schedule with randomized jitter and a soft-priority earmark for telemetry-only probes.
Motivation: previous heuristics used a fixed delay and naive probing which led to oscillation when many tenants attempted to reestablish connections at the same time. The change reduces cascading pressure during regional restore and gives SLO enforcers a wider window to rebalance.
What changed (high level):
- introduced pkg/failover/adaptive_delay.go: new controller that exposes a small API to compute region-level rejoin delay given metrics (kv_pressure, recent_reopens).
- added sticky probe state to serving/probe_manager.go with per-tenant backoff state persisted in memory and optionally in the KV snapshot for cross-controller continuity.
- SLO enforcement integration: slo/enforcer now consults adaptive_delay for early decision to defer low-priority requests during rejoin windows.
- telemetry: standardized two new metrics (region_rejoin_delay_seconds, tenant_probe_attempt{reason=\"sticky\"}) and a tag for kv_pressure_level.
- config: feature-flagged rollout via config/feature_flags.yaml and operator-visible knobs in console UI.
- hotfix: corrected a metric name mismatch that caused alerts to miss soft reopen spikes (alert: reopen-spike-soft was firing after the incident due to misnamed metric).
Implementation notes:
- adaptive_delay computes a baseDelay = min( maxDelay, defaultDelay * (1 + kvPressureFactor) * reopenDecayFactor ) where kvPressureFactor is a small linear scale from 0..2 derived from recent KV write latency/queue depth. reopenDecayFactor decays with an exponential moving average of reopen attempts in the last 5 minutes.
- sticky probing uses a per-tenant window with exponential backoff (initial 10s, multiplier 1.8, cap 10m) and randomized jitter +/-20%. Probe attempts mark themselves as telemetry_only when the tenant is in low-priority cohort to avoid promoter traffic.
- All new behavior behind feature flag: failover.adaptive_delay.enabled and probe.sticky_enabled.
Rollout plan:
- feature flag off by default in main.
- canary: enable for 5% of traffic in us-west-2 for 48 hours while watching region_rejoin_delay_seconds and kv_pressure_level.
- if stable, ramp to 50% then 100% over 72 hours.
- if kv_pressure or SLO violation delta exceeds the rollback threshold, toggle off and iterate.
Testing:
- unit tests cover adaptive_delay edge cases (max/min, negative pressure).
- integration test simulates 100 tenants with staggered evictions and verifies median reopen latency improves and fewer kv queue spikes.
- e2e canary run executed against staging; flaky test integration.test_rejoin_probe retried once and passed.
Backwards compatibility & migration:
- feature flag guard prevents behavior change until explicitly enabled.
- metric rename included mapping in telemetry migration doc so alert rules will not break during rollout.
Related work: builds on ENG-4123 (failure domain stabilization), references earlier tenant-probe work (ENG-198).
Urgency: hotfix to prevent recurrence of the previously observed reopen storm; recommended to canary ASAP in staging and schedule a controlled rollout.
